item.text:
1. **(a) Structural error: the level-0 pattern is sufficient, not necessary.**  
   An unramified quadratic factor need not have irreducible quadratic reduction when its generator is non-maximal. For example, with \(u=3\), a nonsquare modulo \(7\),
   \[
   F(x)=(x^2-49u)(x^3-7).
   \]
   The quadratic factor generates the unramified quadratic extension \(\mathbb Q_7(\sqrt u)\), and \(x^3-7\) is totally ramified cubic, so \(F\) has type \(\{(1,2),(3,1)\}\). But
   \[
   \bar F(x)=x^5,
   \]
   not \(\bar q(x)x^3\) with \(\bar q\) irreducible. Thus the stated pattern identifies one valid branch, but it is not exhaustive for the type. When that pattern does occur, the irreducible quadratic does Hensel-lift as claimed; standard Hensel/Newton-polygon background is catalogued in these [MIT notes](https://math.mit.edu/~roed/courses/18.782/lectures.html).

2. **(b) Correct, conditional on entering the displayed cubic branch.**  
   Iterating integer-slope repeated-linear residuals versus a denominator-\(3\) slope or a splitting residual is the right exhaustive structure. A reduced denominator \(3\) forces the entire degree-three cluster to be one ramification-index-\(3\) factor. The repeated-linear loop is possible at \(p=7\). The tame binomial/Kummer description is also appropriate; tame extensions have the stated radical form in these [Stanford local-field notes](https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/mordellsem/Notes/L08.pdf).

3. **(c) Correct.**  
   For an irreducible totally ramified quintic, the residue degree is \(1\), so all conjugates have the same residue and the reduction must be
   \[
   (x-\bar c)^5.
   \]
   In characteristic \(5\), this equals \(x^5-\bar c^{\,5}\). The phrase “plus multiples of \(5\)” belongs to the lifts over \(\mathbb Z_5\), not literally to polynomials over \(\mathbb F_5\).

4. **(d) Structural error in the asserted \((1,1)\)-vertex exit.**  
   After recentering, the linear coefficient is
   \[
   f'(c)=5c^4+4a_4c^3+3a_3c^2+2a_2c+a_1,
   \]
   not merely \(5c^4\). All terms are divisible by \(5\), but cancellation can raise the valuation. A jump in \(v(f(c))\) does not force \(v(f'(c))=1\). Explicitly,
   \[
   f(x)=x^5-5x+29,\qquad \bar f=(x-1)^5,
   \]
   yet
   \[
   f(x+1)=x^5+5x^4+10x^3+10x^2+25.
   \]
   The constant has valuation \(2\), while the linear coefficient is zero; the lower polygon has a vertex at \((2,1)\), not \((1,1)\), and gives a \(2+3\)-shaped exit rather than the claimed \(1+4\) shape. The abstract exit/loop/target trichotomy remains reasonable, but the highlighted exit must be described as a subcase requiring \(v(f'(c))=1\).

5. **(e) Correct, with the usual cancellation qualification.**  
   The four middle coefficients \(5,10,10,5\) have valuation exactly \(1\), so recentering contributes carry terms one level below; sums of those contributions may cancel and fall still deeper. Also,
   \[
   u\in\mathbb Z_5^\times \text{ is a fifth power }
   \Longleftrightarrow
   u\bmod25 \text{ is a fifth power in }(\mathbb Z/25)^\times.
   \]
   Here “one mod \(25\)” must mean “a fifth power mod \(25\),” not “congruent to \(1\).”

6. **(f) Correct only for a genuinely regenerative one-state loop.**  
   Then summing exits at depths \(k\) gives \(WE\sum L^k=WE/(1-L)\). Frobenius regenerates the residual *shape*, but by itself does not prove that carry states have one fixed scalar \(L,E\); that requires the suppressed carry calculation. Without lumpability, the natural expression is a matrix resolvent \(W(I-M)^{-1}E\). Moreover, because finding 1 omits additional tame entry branches, the displayed single-\(W_{\mathrm{first}}\) series cannot represent the full tame density as written.

**VERDICT: FAIL (2)** — the two definite structural errors are the necessity claim in (a) and the forced \((1,1)\)-vertex claim in (d).
